science: Root read actual final apparatus, source/oracle, vector equilibrium plus deposited-charge Poisson reference, grader, validator, AUTHOR, input/history/provenance records, local/scientific reports and peer. Source differentiates exact laboratory polarization but omits the moving material electrode contribution. Physical upper-electrode charge follows the third material offset.
public_input_review: Complete cell energy includes internal electrostatics. Shorted material faces, neutral termination, conventional current sign, reference-area normalization, complete relaxation, domains and limits close the apparatus. Exact unrestricted neutral instruction and standard image boundary exclude private repair, hints, grader and oracle. No public fitted default or parameter leak.
calibration_review: 288 fixed-sigma .001 records at 18 longitudinal settings. Source and physical readout agree. The stated derivative and equilibrium bounds prove monotone identification of K on the full interval; 41 noiseless fits recover within 8.38e-9.
grading_review: All 256 noisy fits satisfy calibration and parameter gates; all oracle groups pass and all three shortcut diagnostic groups fail. Maximum oracle error .000242, minimum shortcut error .4888. Full-K gaps exceed .37498. Independent reference agrees within 8.62e-12 over 2368 domain cases. Local oracle 7/7 in .625s, shortcut 4 passes and 3 intended failures in .606s; science validation 17.758s.
qualifications: The integrated electrode charge is naturally exact under charge/first-moment-preserving deposition; mesh checks do not claim microscopic field resolution. Extended arbitrary-frame and rotation checks are unscored and outside the public upper-triangular domain. Numerical grids are bounded evidence. The nonlinear classical constitutive energy is author-supplied, not attributed to Vanderbilt.
classification_caveat: Retaining the polarization-density readout may be a physical failure. Correct transported-electrode-charge reasoning followed by sign, normal, determinant, derivative, index or solver errors must be classified separately from pure physics failures.
